items.stem: How should administrative rights be granted in a Cursor team?

options.text: To as few people as the work requires (least privilege)
options.rationale: Correct: limiting admin rights limits the blast radius of mistakes or breaches.

options.text: To everyone, so no one is blocked
options.rationale: Broad admin access is a serious security liability.
Access should follow need, not request order.

options.text: Never to anyone, even the owner
options.rationale: Some administration is necessary; it should just be limited.

items.explanation: Correct: limiting admin rights limits the blast radius of mistakes or breaches.

items.stem: Which TWO actions matter most when a team member leaves? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: prompt revocation closes an open door.

options.text: Review what access and tokens they held
options.rationale: Correct: knowing their access guides what to rotate or revoke.

options.text: Leave their account active in case they return
options.rationale: An active departed account is an open risk.

options.text: Share their token with the team
options.rationale: Reusing a personal token defeats auditing and rotation.

items.explanation: Correct: prompt revocation closes an open door.

items.stem: You need to confirm whether a sensitive repo's data is handled privately. What should you do?

options.text: Check the actual data and privacy settings rather than assume
options.rationale: Correct: privacy must be verified in the settings, not assumed.
Defaults may not match your privacy need.

options.text: Ask a teammate what they think it does
Disable all logging to be safe

items.explanation: Correct: privacy must be verified in the settings, not assumed.
